title: V NDE 3928
content: I remember it being a lovely day, weather-wise, and I was very happy that my mother was allowing me to take a nap in my parent's bed, rather than my own, which was on the floor and hard. Their bed was nice and soft, and high, they had pillows, and I loved it. I knew I should lie down and go to sleep, but I was too excited. I started jumping up and down on the bed, and noticed there was a bottle of medicine on the (very tall) bureau, next to the bed. I tried to see if I could reach it. I could. I knew I shouldn't touch it, but I did. Then I began playing doctor and patient. The doctor in me would prescribe, and the patient in me would take the pills. This continued until the bottle was empty. I don't remember passing out. I do remember suddenly seeing myself from above. In the middle of the bed, on my side, legs and arms positioned as though I was running. I didn't feel anything in particular about being out of my body nor looking at myself. I remember, clearly, thinking that it was funny that I looked as though I was running when I was actually 'sleeping'. Suddenly, I was 'sucked backwards' (at warp speed), as though 'through the roof'. Then the blackest black - nothingness. I saw no tunnel, no light - just blackness. It didn't inspire fear. I felt perfectly fine, and somewhat like a detached observer. Everything seemed to be happening to quickly, I didn't have time to think. Then, I was Home. Earth and this life were a bad summer camp, in comparison, and I knew I wanted to stay. I didn't want to go back to camp. That's all I knew. I didn't 'see 'God,' but I felt as though I was sitting in the lap and wrapped in the arms of the most wonderful, loving (giant) 'parent'. This is where it gets frustrating, because there are not, now, and will never be words to convey how this feels. I detest using the word 'God' because of the great perversion we humans have made of the concept, but I will use it from this point onward, merely for the sake of expedience. I was 'sitting in God's lap', wrapped in the warmest embrace, and immediately involved in a 'conversation'. We communicated telepathically. I don't know how else to describe it. I didn't want to come back. That was my focus. I was Home, I liked being Home, just let me be Home. God was holding me tighter (in the best of ways), and showing me the life to which I must return. My field of vision was akin to being inside a TV screen watching a movie. Though I knew, then, that it's what happens, I was three. How much could I have done? The only thing I can remember in terms of a 'life review' is seeing myself standing at my baby brother's crib, on a chair, looking down at him. In terms of emotional attachment, he could have been an uninteresting rock in a pile of uninteresting rocks. I felt nothing, and that 'made God cry,' which is literally Hell. Immediately, I knew that love is the only important thing. At different points throughout the experience, I would suddenly know massive amounts of information. Again, this is difficult to describe in words. Words seem more a blockade. After making God cry (and I say that in good humor) my life was shown to me in the form of a long road - and it didn't look like a road I'd choose to travel (though I knew I HAD chosen the road). I saw many of the different places I'd live and people I'd know. Jobs. Experiences. Too much sadness. I didn't want it. But God just kept gently showing me that I was going back. The movie kept running and the road kept going - so fast - so much 'information' that was both, personal and universal. Most of the information was about Thought and Love. Way down the road, late in my life, it seemed the trip would become more enjoyable. God told me (crappy earth translation ahead) to stay true, 'follow the clues', and all would be well. The totality of God's love for me was the predominant feeling/understanding, at all times (luckily, that feeling has stayed with me, though I don't necessarily understand it, any more). The next thing I remember is sitting in the front seat of the car, between my parents, leaving the hospital.

tunnel.passage_other_detail: Described being 'sucked backwards' 'through the roof' at 'warp speed' into 'the blackest black - nothingness' with 'no tunnel, no light'.

arrival.other_being_detail: Felt like being held by a loving 'giant parent' and later refers to this presence as 'God' for convenience.

boundary_and_return.mission_detail: God told the experiencer to “stay true, 'follow the clues', and all would be well.”

context.nde_cause_other_detail: Accidental ingestion/overdose of medicine/pills as a child while playing (“playing doctor and patient… until the bottle was empty”).

stage_sequence.elements_other_detail: Includes rapid backward movement into blackness/void and a strong 'Home' sense with a loving parental presence identified as God; life shown as a 'movie' and 'long road'.
stage_sequence.sequence_variation_description: OBE → rapid backward movement/void (no tunnel/light) → 'Home' with God/presence and telepathic communication → brief life review/life preview → return (next memory in car leaving hospital).

unique_elements.nonstandard_elements: No tunnel or light; transition described as being 'sucked backwards' at 'warp speed' into 'the blackest black - nothingness'. God experienced as a giant loving parent holding the experiencer in a lap/embrace; vision like being inside a TV screen; life shown as a 'long road' already chosen.
unique_elements.notable_quotes: “sucked backwards (at warp speed), as though 'through the roof'.” “Then the blackest black - nothingness. I saw no tunnel, no light - just blackness.” “Then, I was Home. Earth and this life were a bad summer camp, in comparison…” “I was 'sitting in God's lap', wrapped in the warmest embrace…” “We communicated telepathically.” “there are not, now, and will never be words to convey how this feels.” “Immediately, I knew that love is the only important thing.” “follow the clues”
